- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for overreaction.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, add 0.5–1.5% to each day’s forecast to correct for underestimation.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7) and forecast is smooth, introduce 1–2% noise or slight trend reversal to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimistic tail-end forecasts; cap final 3–5 days at 1–2% below recent 10-day average to prevent overshoot.
